topic: 7 strange borders countdown ending on the Cooch Behar enclaves
hook: Your map once held a patch of India inside Bangladesh inside India inside Bangladesh, and it was completely real.
title: 7 Borders That Make Zero Sense (India's Is Wildest)
description:
Seven real borders that look fake on a map, from a lake with no agreed border to an island where you can see China's skyline from Taiwanese land. The countdown ends on India's strangest border of all, the Cooch Behar enclaves that were swapped with Bangladesh in 2015. Watch to the end for a patch of land that sat inside three layers of other countries.

#borders #geography #india
comment_prompt: Which border was the strangest for you?

scenes.narration: Your map once held a patch of India inside Bangladesh inside India inside Bangladesh, and it was completely real.
scenes.headline: India Inside Bangladesh

scenes.narration: That is one of seven borders in this video that make no sense, and each one is stranger than the last.
scenes.headline: Seven Strange Borders

scenes.narration: We start with a lake where nobody ever agreed on a line, and we end on India's strangest border.
scenes.headline: From Lake To India

scenes.narration: Along the way, you will see a town you can only reach by driving through another country.
scenes.headline: Drive Through Another Country

scenes.narration: You will see a runway that cuts across a road, and an island where you can see China from Taiwanese land.
scenes.headline: Runway Across A Road

scenes.narration: By the end, you will know how Indian villagers once lived on land that was stuck inside a foreign country.
scenes.headline: Stuck Inside A Foreign Country

scenes.narration: Let's start with number seven, in the middle of Europe, on a lake you may have seen on holiday postcards.
scenes.headline: Number Seven

scenes.narration: Number seven: Lake Constance, a huge lake in the Alps that touches Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
scenes.headline: Lake Constance

scenes.narration: Three countries share its shores, and they have never signed a treaty that fixes the border through the water.
scenes.headline: No Treaty On The Water

scenes.narration: Look at a map and you will find a blank space on the water, right where a border line should be.
scenes.headline: A Blank On The Map

scenes.narration: Austria has long argued that the whole lake is shared. Others see it differently, so the line stays missing.
scenes.headline: Nobody Agrees

scenes.narration: So how do they run the lake? They agree on rules for boats and fishing, not on borders.
scenes.headline: Rules, Not Borders

scenes.narration: Imagine a cricket ground where the boundary rope was never laid, yet everyone keeps playing and nobody argues.
scenes.headline: A Ground Without A Rope

scenes.narration: That is a border that works only because everyone is polite, and it has worked for a very long time.
scenes.headline: A Polite Border

scenes.narration: That one is calm. The next border is perfectly clear on a map, and that is exactly the problem.
scenes.headline: A Clear Line, A Big Problem

scenes.narration: Number six: Point Roberts, a small town in Washington state, on the American side of the map.
scenes.headline: Point Roberts

scenes.narration: Here is the twist: you cannot drive there from the rest of America without crossing Canada first.
scenes.headline: Through Canada To Reach USA

scenes.narration: The border follows the 49th parallel, and the tip of this peninsula landed just south of that line.
scenes.headline: The 49th Parallel

scenes.narration: So the town is American land, but the only road to it by land runs through Canada.
scenes.headline: American Land, Canadian Road

scenes.narration: To get there from Seattle, you leave the United States, cross Canada, and then enter the United States again.
scenes.headline: Leave, Cross, Re-Enter

scenes.narration: Think of reaching your own house only by passing through your neighbour's compound, with a guard at both gates.
scenes.headline: Two Gates, Two Guards

scenes.narration: The road is real, the border posts are real, and the town is real. It just sits on the wrong side of a line.
scenes.headline: Wrong Side Of The Line

scenes.narration: Point Roberts shows that a line can be perfectly clear on paper and still make everyday life odd.
scenes.headline: Clear Line, Odd Life

scenes.narration: And if that feels strange, wait until you meet a Spanish town that is stuck inside France.
scenes.headline: A Spanish Town In France

scenes.narration: Number five: Llívia, a Spanish town that sits completely inside France, with French land on every side.
scenes.headline: Llívia

scenes.narration: In 1659, Spain and France signed a treaty that handed France a list of villages in the Pyrenees.
scenes.headline: The Treaty Of 1659

scenes.narration: Llívia was a town, not a village, so it was never on the list, and it stayed Spanish.
scenes.headline: A Town, Not A Village

scenes.narration: A single word in a treaty from 1659 still decides which flag flies over its streets today.
scenes.headline: One Word, One Flag

scenes.narration: A short road links it to the rest of Spain, and that road is treated as neutral ground.
scenes.headline: The Neutral Road

scenes.narration: Walk out of town in any other direction and you are in France, with French road signs and French village names.
scenes.headline: France On Every Side

scenes.narration: It is a tiny place, but it proves that a border can survive just because someone read a treaty very carefully.
scenes.headline: A Careful Reading

scenes.narration: Remember this: a border does not need to make sense, it only needs to be written down.
scenes.headline: Written Down, So It Stays

scenes.narration: Next, a village that is German on paper, yet sits inside a Swiss world of francs and customs.
scenes.headline: German Village, Swiss World

scenes.narration: Number four: Büsingen am Hochrhein, a German village surrounded on every side by Switzerland.
scenes.headline: Büsingen

scenes.narration: It follows German law, but for customs purposes it counts as part of Switzerland.
scenes.headline: German Law, Swiss Customs

scenes.narration: Shops here accept Swiss francs and euros, so your change might come back in either currency.
scenes.headline: Francs And Euros

scenes.narration: Many people there live like their Swiss neighbours, working and shopping just across the line.
scenes.headline: Living Like A Neighbour

scenes.narration: Its odd position goes back centuries, to deals between rulers long before modern passports even existed.
scenes.headline: A Centuries-Old Deal

scenes.narration: So its people follow one country's laws, use two currencies, and live inside another country's land.
scenes.headline: One Village, Two Worlds

scenes.narration: If strange maps like these are your thing, subscribe now. Number three is where a runway cuts a road in two.
scenes.headline: Subscribe For More

scenes.narration: Number three: Gibraltar airport, where a runway cuts straight across a busy public road.
scenes.headline: Gibraltar Airport

scenes.narration: Gibraltar is a British territory at the southern tip of Spain, and the Spanish border sits right beside the airport.
scenes.headline: British Land, Spanish Border

scenes.narration: The main road into town, Winston Churchill Avenue, crosses the runway itself, with no bridge and no tunnel.
scenes.headline: The Road Crosses The Runway

scenes.narration: When a plane is about to land or take off, barriers come down and the road closes to cars and walkers.
scenes.headline: Barriers Come Down

scenes.narration: Think of a railway crossing in an Indian town, only the train is an airplane.
scenes.headline: A Railway Gate For Planes

scenes.narration: Cars wait, scooters wait, people wait with shopping bags, and then the jet roars past right in front of them.
scenes.headline: Everyone Waits For The Jet

scenes.narration: Anyone walking in from Spain has to cross the runway to reach the town on the other side.
scenes.headline: Walk Across A Runway

scenes.narration: A border post and an airport are squeezed into the same tiny patch of ground, and they share it politely.
scenes.headline: Border And Airport Together

scenes.narration: Gibraltar is so small that the runway takes up a big part of the flat land it has.
scenes.headline: A Tiny Flat Space

scenes.narration: Now we reach the top two, and both are places where the border is very close to you.
scenes.headline: The Top Two

scenes.narration: Number two: Kinmen, an island run by Taiwan, but only a few kilometres from the Chinese city of Xiamen.
scenes.headline: Kinmen
scenes.sub: Taiwan, a few km from China

scenes.narration: Take a boat there, and from Taiwanese land you can see China's skyline across the water.
scenes.headline: China's Skyline From Taiwan

scenes.narration: Xiamen's tall buildings stand on the horizon, while Kinmen's beaches are lined with old steel anti-landing spikes.
scenes.headline: Towers And Spikes

scenes.narration: Kinmen is much farther from Taiwan's own main island than it is from China, yet it belongs to Taiwan's government.
scenes.headline: Closer To China

scenes.narration: In 1958, China began a heavy artillery bombardment of Kinmen, and shelling went on for years afterwards.
scenes.headline: The 1958 Shelling

scenes.narration: Today, people on Kinmen make knives from steel taken from old shell casings, and tourists buy them as souvenirs.
scenes.headline: Knives From Shells

scenes.narration: Since 2001, ferries have run between Kinmen and Xiamen, so a short boat ride now links two places that once exchanged fire.
scenes.headline: A Ferry Since 2001

scenes.narration: Picture standing on one beach, seeing a modern Chinese city, and knowing the border is just that thin strip of water.
scenes.headline: A Border Made Of Water

scenes.narration: There is no fence and no painted line here, just open sea, and you can see the other side with your own eyes.
scenes.headline: No Fence, Just Sea

scenes.narration: For people in Kinmen, China is not a headline, it is the view from the beach.
scenes.headline: China Is The View

scenes.narration: The two sides see their future very differently, yet the water between them stays only a few kilometres wide.
scenes.headline: A Few Kilometres Apart

scenes.narration: But number one is stranger than all of these, and it is right here in India.
scenes.headline: Number One Is In India

scenes.narration: Number one: the enclaves of Cooch Behar, India's strangest border of all, on the edge of Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Cooch Behar Enclaves

scenes.narration: For decades, the India-Bangladesh border here was a jigsaw puzzle of small patches, each belonging to the other country.
scenes.headline: A Jigsaw Border

scenes.narration: An Indian village could be surrounded by Bangladesh, and a Bangladeshi village could sit deep inside West Bengal.
scenes.headline: Villages In Foreign Land

scenes.narration: These patches were called enclaves, and before 2015 there were 111 Indian ones inside Bangladesh and 51 Bangladeshi ones inside India.
scenes.headline: Enclaves Before 2015

scenes.narration: One legend says it began with a chess game between two local rulers, who bet villages on the result.
scenes.headline: The Chess Game Legend

scenes.narration: Whatever the cause, people in these patches lived in limbo, often cut off from schools, electricity and hospitals.
scenes.headline: Living In Limbo

scenes.narration: To reach their own country, many had to cross a foreign border first, and their own officials often could not reach them.
scenes.headline: A Foreign Border In The Way

scenes.narration: And then came the truly crazy bit, a plot of land called Dahala Khagrabari.
scenes.headline: Dahala Khagrabari

scenes.narration: It was a tiny piece of India, inside a piece of Bangladesh, inside a piece of India, inside Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Four Layers Deep

scenes.narration: Map experts often described it as the only one of its kind in the world.
scenes.headline: One Of A Kind

scenes.narration: A farmer there was in India, but to reach the Indian mainland he had to cross several borders in a row.
scenes.headline: Several Borders To Go Home

scenes.narration: At midnight on 31 July 2015, India and Bangladesh finally swapped these patches under a land boundary agreement.
scenes.headline: Midnight, 31 July 2015

scenes.narration: Residents were given a choice of country, and many people finally became citizens of the land they had always lived on.
scenes.headline: Finally A Citizen

scenes.narration: For the first time, many of them could get roads, electricity and schools from the country around them.
scenes.headline: Roads, Power, Schools

scenes.narration: That is India's strangest border: a puzzle of tiny patches that took nearly seventy years to untangle.
scenes.headline: Nearly 70 Years To Untangle

scenes.narration: Think about it: a border is usually a line on a map, but here it was pieces of two countries mixed together.
scenes.headline: Pieces Of Two Countries

scenes.narration: So India's strangest border is not a wall or a fence. It was a tangle of tiny lands that nobody could reach.
scenes.headline: A Tangle Of Tiny Lands

scenes.narration: Seven borders, seven different ways a map can go strange, and the wildest one was sitting in India all along.
scenes.headline: Seven Ways A Map Goes Strange

scenes.narration: And that is why your map once held a patch of India inside Bangladesh inside India inside Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Back To The Start

scenes.headline: Next: The 15-Minute Border
